The recovery ZIP was re-extracted fresh, its requirements installed, and its test suite run before anything else; the tested playbook then drove the run. No ClickUp sync, SharePoint/GitHub/API publish, HUD script, or new schedule was touched, and no extra test email was sent — the existing monthly schedule (10th, 8:00 AM America/Los_Angeles) is unchanged.

**Research**
41 isolated workflow agents re-researched every existing market-rate comparable row for every requested bedroom type against current public sources. 36 submitted on the first pass; the five that exhausted their turn budget (13 – Jefferson, 18 – Opa Locka, 48 – Coral Village, 53 – Bayou Pointe, 28 – Granite Ridge) were recovered in a five-agent recovery run rather than re-running the whole set.

**Coverage — 499 requested cells across 190 comparable rows**
257 numeric source-supported base rents, 129 Phone Verify, 113 evidenced Not Offered. 29 property/bedroom groups closed with no numeric coverage, so their market average reads Phone Verify instead of an old average.

**Conservative review applied (28 exclusions, zero prices introduced)**
Seven price cells were excluded: three were arithmetic derivations of a fee-inclusive total rather than a published base rent (Waterford Pointe, two Manor Homes plans); Copper Ridge/Bellaview's 1BD and 2BD were pulled after the public PBRA/affordable record conflicted with the August 2026 sale; Broadcast Center's 1BD was pulled for unconfirmed unit-level status in a mixed-income LIHTC property; 702 Fleer Rd was pulled because the operator page says the home is no longer available. Twenty-one Not Offered findings were withheld on comps whose identity or eligibility stayed unresolved, and five thin-market single-unit supplements were adjudicated to market-rate with their comparability limits documented.

The build returned "SUCCESSFUL WITH COVERAGE LIMITS; REVIEW REQUIRED" and the readback pass was a REAL REPORT READBACK PASS: 499 cells structurally verified, 234 benchmark/summary tie-outs, 35,797 styles preserved, 34,042 untouched cell values unchanged, source workbook byte-identical, no prohibited pricing evidence, no eligibility conflicts. Automation is live and verified. Rather than create a second schedule — which would have produced two competing reports each month — I inspected the existing one and repaired it in place.

**Live configuration** (task `9Ap8dG4ztrNsH94FP2Q6UC`, "ApartmentCorp Monthly Rent Comp Report")

Monthly on day 10 at 08:00 America/Los_Angeles, status active, full-auto, run-as-new-task, attached to the Reports project so every run inherits the recovery ZIP. Exactly one schedule exists, so there is no duplicate send risk. Next run: **November 10, 2026, 8:00 AM PT**.

**What was actually broken and is now fixed**

The timing was already right, but the schedule's playbook still described the retired pipeline: run `find_comps_v2.py`, `build_excel.py`, and `clickup_sync.py`, then push 42 properties into ClickUp. Had it fired on the 10th, it would have executed the obsolete HUD pipeline and synced ClickUp. That text is gone, replaced with the workflow we proved today: recover the package from the project ZIP, extract the manifest from the approved baseline, research every existing comparable through workflow agents, review conservatively, build only with genuine current observations, verify via `verify_report.py`, render the checklist PDF, then send from apartmentcorp44@gmail.com to exactly your two recipients and inspect Sent afterward.

**Two safeguards added from today's evidence**

The run exposed a real failure mode: five of 41 research agents burned their 43-turn budget without submitting. The playbook now caps each agent at two to three tool calls per comparable, requires a phone_verify submission instead of an omitted row, and mandates a recovery pass over only the failed properties — never a full re-run, which would double the cost. Separately, a single 41-agent workflow can trigger an interactive budget approval that an unattended run cannot grant, so the playbook now instructs batching at 18 properties or fewer when confirmation is unavailable.

**What each run will enforce**

Sender and recipient set are fixed and re-verified at send time; the subject pattern is `ApartmentCorp Rent Comps — Monthly Fresh Refresh [Month YYYY]`; the build fails closed on stale evidence, missing coverage, checksum mismatch, prohibited pricing evidence, or wholly Phone Verify research; the receipt records message ID and file checksums; and Sent is inspected before any retry so an ambiguous failure cannot become a duplicate email. A failed run records the failure rather than emailing the August workbook as if it were new.

One thing worth your judgment later: the run date sits on the 10th, but research agents will see whatever listings are live that morning, so a comp that vanishes mid-month shows as Phone Verify until the next cycle. That is the honest outcome, but it means month-to-month averages can dip for reasons that are about listing churn rather than rent movement.
